summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs is reportedly moving toward revoking the 2001 maritime MoU with Cambodia. Officials argue that since Cambodia joined the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) in February 2026, a 'new legal reality' exists. Thailand intends to shift away from bilateral negotiations toward this international legal framework to resolve the long-standing deadlock over the 26,000-square-kilometer Overlapping Claims Area.
title: Thailand eyes UN maritime law to resolve Cambodia border dispute

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn announced that Cambodia will use international law and peaceful mechanisms to handle maritime disputes if Thailand unilaterally cancels the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). He stated that the MoU is currently the only shared framework for managing overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand and its removal would force Cambodia to explore other legal avenues to protect its sovereignty.
title: Cambodia to seek legal solutions if Thailand exits maritime pact

summary: Thai authorities at the Khlong Luek border checkpoint repatriated 55 Cambodian migrant workers (34 men, 19 women, and 2 boys) after their legal cases were finalized. The operation involved coordination between the Burapha Task Force, border patrol, immigration, and health officials to ensure a structured return process.
title: Thailand repatriates 55 Cambodian workers via border

summary: Acting Head of State Hun Sen warned that Thailand's push to cancel the 2001 maritime MoU (MOU 44) could dismantle the long-standing bilateral framework for managing overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand. Citing Thai security experts, he suggested the move is driven by nationalism and questioned if it is an attempt to 'internationalize' the dispute. He expressed respect for Thai analysts who oppose the cancellation and warned that moving away from bilateral talks could complicate future negotiations.
title: Hun Sen warns Thai move to end maritime MoU may fuel row

summary: Cambodian analysts have rejected claims made by the Thai Ambassador to the UN regarding historical assistance to Cambodia. They argue that Thailand is using past aid, including $17 million in technical assistance since COVID-19, to justify current 'aggression' and violations of sovereignty. The report highlights that thousands of Cambodian households remain displaced near the border due to Thai blockades and explosive remnants of war.
title: Experts reject Thai claims of past aid to justify actions against Cambodia

summary: CMAC deminers report that border tensions are complicating efforts to clear landmines. Officials state that new cluster munitions have been fired into areas previously cleared, creating 'newly affected zones' and delaying the goal to be mine-free by 2030.
title: 85% of homes cleared, but farmland still at risk of blasts

summary: Phnom Penh has warned it will shift from bilateral negotiations to international legal mechanisms under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) if Thailand unilaterally withdraws from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding. Kung Phoak, Secretary of State at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that Cambodia is prepared to invoke 'compulsory conciliation' to resolve overlapping maritime claims. This comes as the Thai Cabinet is expected to meet today to discuss a proposal to scrap the pact.
title: Cambodia signals UNCLOS route if Thailand scraps maritime MoU

summary: Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn announced that Cambodia will trigger a 'compulsory conciliation' process under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). This comes after the Thai Cabinet officially voted to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 44) regarding overlapping maritime claims. Cambodia expressed 'deep regret,' stating the MoU was the only bilateral framework for peaceful negotiation and that Thailand's withdrawal undermines the spirit of cooperation.
title: Sea you in court: Cambodia announces UNCLOS conciliation as Thais exit maritime MoU

summary: Banteay Meanchey provincial officials are accelerating the construction of temporary housing and providing agricultural aid to thousands of civilians displaced by border tensions with Thailand. Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that Prime Minister Hun Manet is prioritizing the welfare of affected families and veterans, with nearly 3,000 housing units already completed in Banteay Meanchey to provide safe accommodation while the border issue is resolved through diplomacy.
title: Shelters expanded for thousands still displaced

summary: Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn stated that Phnom Penh has 'no option' but to trigger the compulsory conciliation mechanism under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). This follows the Thai Cabinet's decision to withdraw from the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) regarding joint energy exploration in the Gulf of Thailand. Sokhonn expressed regret over the unilateral move, noting that the MOU was the only bilateral framework for resolving the dispute.
title: Cambodia to seek UN intervention over maritime claims after Thailand withdraws from agreement

summary: Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn issued a statement clarifying that Thailand's move to scrap the maritime pact does not change Cambodia's legal claims over its waters. He expressed regret that Thailand abandoned a framework that existed for 25 years but reassured the public that Cambodia remains committed to international legal standards to safeguard its sovereignty.
title: Foreign Minister: Thailand's Termination of MoU 2001 Does Not Affect Cambodia's Lawful Rights

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet announced that Cambodia will turn to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) for compulsory conciliation. This comes after Thailand's cabinet unilaterally decided to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU 44) regarding maritime boundaries. The PM stated this is necessary to protect Cambodia's interests and find a peaceful solution through international law since the bilateral agreement has been rejected by Bangkok.
title: Cambodia to Pursue UNCLOS Conciliation After Thailand Withdraws from MOU 2001, PM Hun Manet Says

summary: The Thai Cabinet has approved the cancellation of the 2001 maritime MoU with Cambodia, seeking a new negotiation framework under international law. Thai spokesperson Ratchada Thanadirek stated that the move is a 'realignment' to reflect modern realities and will proceed under the UNCLOS framework to ensure more systematic results.
title: Thailand scraps maritime agreement with Cambodia, turns to UNCLOS framework

summary: A sharp editorial criticizes recent Thai military actions near the O'Smach border crossing, alleging that Thai forces are using noisy distractions and 'word games' to obscure increased military presence. The piece claims that on April 29, Thai activities significantly increased border tensions and calls for a firm Cambodian stance against what it describes as provocative behavior that undermines the existing fragile peace along the 817-kilometer border.
title: Editorial: "Firecrackers cannot hide the truth at O'Smach gate"

source: វិមាន7មករា (CPP Party News)
summary: In Banteay Meanchey province, Cambodia officially welcomed a new Head of Mission for the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT), Rear Admiral Glenn Z. Dizon from the Philippines. Lt. Gen. Phat Vibolsopheak reiterated Cambodia's full cooperation with the observers to verify and maintain the ceasefire along the border. The government emphasized its commitment to the 2025 Joint Statement of the General Border Committee (GBC) to maintain peace following previous border tensions and fighting.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Full Support for AOT to Ensure Ceasefire Implementation Along Border with Thailand

summary: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., acting as ASEAN Chair, organized a trilateral meeting in Cebu on May 7, 2026, with Cambodian PM Hun Manet and Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul. The leaders shook hands and vowed to pursue peace and rebuild trust following deadly border clashes in 2025. PM Hun Manet reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to peaceful legal solutions, while PM Anutin acknowledged that war only brings loss. The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) mandate was extended until July to monitor the border.
title: ASEAN Chair Philippines shows effectiveness in mediating end to Thailand-Cambodia conflict

summary: On Wednesday, Cambodia held a briefing for foreign diplomats and international organizations regarding Thailand's unilateral decision to cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on overlapping maritime claims. Prime Minister Hun Manet expressed 'deep regret' over the move, stating it abandons the only bilateral framework used for over 20 years. Consequently, Cambodia announced it will pursue a 'compulsory conciliation' mechanism under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to resolve the dispute fairly.
title: Cambodia briefs diplomats on Thailand's scrapping of maritime MOU

summary: Following a trilateral summit in Cebu with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Cambodia and Thailand have agreed to use the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to resolve maritime disputes in the Overlapping Claims Area (OCA). A high-ranking Cambodian official confirmed that Thailand acknowledged Cambodia's diplomatic note from May 6, which initiated compulsory conciliation after Bangkok unilaterally scrapped the 2001 MoU on maritime claims. However, Cambodia notes it has yet to receive a formal notification from Thailand regarding the MoU termination under the Vienna Convention.
title: Thailand acknowledged Cambodia's notification to proceed with the compulsory conciliation mechanism under UNCLOS

summary: Following the ASEAN Summit in Cebu, Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul and Cambodian PM Hun Manet confirmed they are adhering to the 2025 Joint Statement on a ceasefire. Despite the face-to-face meeting facilitated by the Philippines, Anutin clarified that there were no discussions regarding border demarcation or the reopening of border checkpoints. The leaders focused on maintaining a 'positive atmosphere' and using existing JBC and GBC frameworks to manage the relationship while military deployments remain in place.
title: Thai and Cambodian Prime Ministers Uphold Joint Ceasefire Statement, No Talks on Border Demarcation or Checkpoint Opening

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts has strongly condemned Thailand's unilateral decision to register several ancient border temples—including Tamone, Ta Krabei, and K'nar temples—as Thai national monuments. Cambodia declared the registration 'illegal, null and without legal effect,' stating that the sites are situated within sovereign Cambodian territory and that Thailand is attempting to manufacture a false legal appearance to back its territorial claims.
title: Cambodia accuses Thailand of registering occupied temples to bolster border claims

summary: An in-depth commentary published by Fresh News sharply criticized Thailand's Fine Arts Department for registering the Ta Moan temple complex, Ta Krabey Temple, and K'nar Temple as Thai ancient monuments. The piece asserts that domestic registration cannot create sovereignty or override international border treaties like the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 1907 and the MoU 2000. It accuses Thailand of trying to build an 'artificial legitimacy' over Cambodian cultural sites along the border and destabilizing the framework of international border order.
title: Thailand Is Using Khmer Heritage to Create “Artificial Legitimacy”: Is This the Conduct of a Civilized Nation?

summary: Cambodian state media analyzed the aftermath of Thailand's unilateral termination of the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44). The piece argues that because Thailand dismantled the bilateral negotiation framework itself, Thailand's subsequent call for new bilateral talks under UNCLOS is deeply contradictory. Cambodia maintains that international legal processes and structured arbitration should now take over, criticizing Thailand's sudden flip-flop on negotiation mechanisms.
title: Thailand Destroyed the Bilateral Framework—Now Let International Law Work

summary: The Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts of Cambodia issued a strong protest and categorical rejection regarding Thailand's organization of public events, religious ceremonies, and opening of K'nar Temple for mass public visitation. Cambodia maintains that K'nar Temple, alongside Tamone Thom and Ta Krabey, is located entirely within its sovereign territory according to the 1904 and 1907 Franco-Siamese Treaties. The ministry characterized Thailand's actions as an unlawful attempt to create a 'fait accompli' on the ground to back up its occupation by force, declaring these activities null, void, and without legal effect under international law.
title: Cambodia Condemns Thailand's Activities at K'nar Temple as Sovereignty Violation

summary: Following Thailand's unilateral termination of the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding regarding overlapping maritime claims in the Gulf of Thailand on May 5, 2026, reports have surfaced of heightened Thai naval presence, patrols, and provocative military activities in disputed waters. This escalation follows earlier 2025 cross-border clashes that resulted in casualties and displacement, with Cambodia raising concerns over regional stability and Thailand's inconsistent adherence to international law and UNCLOS principles.
title: Thailand Provokes New Military Activities After Revoking the 2001 MOU

summary: The Cambodian government has accused overseas opposition groups of inciting tensions with Thailand for political gain. Officials emphasized that the government remains committed to peaceful negotiations to protect citizens and border stability, despite the current impasse.
title: Opposition lambasted for fuelling Cambodia-Thailand row

summary: Following Thailand's decision to revoke the 2001 maritime agreement (MoU 44), Cambodia has announced it will initiate compulsory conciliation under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Experts believe this legal strategy will help clarify positions and maintain stability despite the shift toward confrontation.
title: Experts back Cambodia's UNCLOS conciliation plan for overlapping maritime claims with Thailand

summary: The Cambodian government has urged Thailand to resume Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) talks following reports of a leadership reshuffle in Bangkok's negotiating team. Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to peaceful demarcation based on historical maps and international legal principles, while rejecting any use of force to alter borders.
title: Thailand reshuffles JBC team amid renewed call for talks

summary: Thai rangers stopped Cambodian villagers from farming in a disputed area in Sa Kaeo province. Thai authorities claimed the activity crossed into Thai territory, while Cambodian soldiers were present at the scene. Both sides reached an initial agreement to halt all activities in the disputed zone until the border can be clearly clarified.
title: Thai rangers halt Cambodian farming activity in Sa Kaeo border area

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence has formally rejected claims by the Thai military that five gunshots were fired by Cambodian forces in the Phnom Bak area of Oddar Meanchey province earlier today. The ministry labeled the accusation as fabricated and intended to cause confusion, urging the Thai side to stop spreading such information.
title: Defence Ministry rejects Thai allegations of gunfire incident near border

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs briefed diplomats on what it calls unlawful Thai activities near disputed border temples, including unauthorized restoration and the installation of Buddha statues, while reaffirming its commitment to peaceful resolution.
title: Cambodia Briefs Diplomatic Corps on Border Cultural Heritage Situation

summary: The spokesperson for the Cambodian Ministry of National Defence strongly rejected a report by Thai media outlet The Nation Thailand alleging that Cambodia had mobilised troops near Thailand's Trat province. The ministry labeled the claims as false information and a distortion intended to mislead public opinion and stir border tensions.
title: Spokesperson Rejects Thai Media Report Alleging Troop Mobilisation Near Trat Border

summary: Cambodia's Minister of National Defence, General Tea Seiha, confirmed the country is open to holding bilateral border meetings with Thailand. This follows signals from the Thai Minister of Defence regarding the potential use of mechanisms like the General Border Committee (GBC) to reduce tensions and restore stability.
title: Cambodia Welcomes Initiative for Border Talks With Thailand, Says Defence Minister

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that border checkpoints with Cambodia will remain shut until Cambodia meets specific conditions set by Thailand. He emphasized that Thailand will not concede on sovereignty and remains firm on its current border policies.
title: Thai PM Anutin reaffirms Thai-Cambodian border crossings remain closed

summary: Cambodia has demanded that Thailand withdraw its troops from disputed border territories, including Phum Chouk Chey, which it claims are being illegally occupied in violation of bilateral agreements.
title: Cambodia demands Thailand withdraw forces from illegally occupied land

summary: At a UN Security Council debate on protecting civilians, Cambodia's representative highlighted concerns regarding Thai military aggression. Meanwhile, Thailand emphasized its commitment to humanitarian principles, sparking further debate over the ongoing border instability and the impact on local civilians.
title: Cambodia brings up Thai aggression as Thailand commits to ‘humanity’

summary: Cambodia has welcomed Thailand's proposal to resume bilateral border talks, including meetings between defense ministers. Meanwhile, the Cambodian Ministry of National Defence denied recent reports from Thai media claiming Cambodia had mobilized troops near Trat province, labeling the allegations as false and misleading.
title: Cambodia welcomes Thai return to negotiating table amid push for stability

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence officially denied allegations that Cambodian soldiers opened fire twice at the Phnom Trop area. The ministry stated that Cambodian forces are following military discipline and urged the Thai side to verify facts and strictly comply with the General Border Committee (GBC) agreements.
title: Cambodian Ministry of Defence denies Thai allegations of firing near Phnom Trop

summary: Thai police responded to Senate President Hun Sen's recent remarks, urging Cambodia to acknowledge that major online scam centres operate within its borders rather than blaming Thailand as a transit route.
title: Thailand urges Cambodia to face facts on scam centres after Hun Sen remarks

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has confirmed that border checkpoints, including Poipet-Aranyaprathet, will remain closed despite significant economic losses. He also dismissed viral online clips claiming a reopening as AI-generated misinformation.
title: Anutin says 'no reopening' of border with Cambodia despite economic strain

summary: Foreign ministers from Cambodia and Thailand are scheduled to meet in the US to discuss reducing ongoing border friction. Experts suggest the meeting is a chance for de-escalation, provided there is concrete action on the ground.
title: Cambodian and Thai foreign ministers to hold talks in US with eye on cutting tensions

summary: Cambodia is considering compulsory conciliation under UNCLOS to resolve maritime boundary disputes and unlock energy resources in the overlapping claims area. Officials state that Thailand unilaterally revoked the 2001 MOU, which prompted this move.
title: Cambodia pursuing UNCLOS compulsory conciliation with Thailand over maritime boundary, shared energy benefits

summary: Diplomatic efforts are intensifying between Cambodia and Thailand following reports of gunfire near Preah Vihear. Cambodia's military requested verification from Thailand after eight gunshots were heard, while an ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) is currently inspecting Banteay Meanchey to investigate claims of Thai incursions and roadblocks.
title: Cambodia and Thailand seek to ease tensions amid gunfire row

summary: Following reported gunfire near the border on May 24, Cambodia and Thailand are stepping up diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions. Cambodian defense officials have requested Thai authorities to investigate the incident, while Thai military representatives have urged adherence to established border committees and peace agreements.
title: Cambodia, Thailand seek to ease tensions amid gunfire row

summary: Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn met with his Thai counterpart at the UN in New York to discuss confidence-building measures and reiterate Cambodia's commitment to a peaceful, diplomatic solution to border tensions.
title: Prak Sokhonn tells Thailand that Cambodia is ready to resolve border issues fairly

summary: Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister Prak Sokhonn and Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow met in New York to discuss confidence-building measures and restoring normal bilateral relations following the spirit of the Cebu Island meeting.
title: កម្ពុជា-ថៃ បន្តជំរុញយន្តការទ្វេភាគីដើម្បីស្តារទំនាក់ទំនងឱ្យកាន់តែប្រសើរឡើងវិញ តាមស្មារតីនៃកិច្ចប្រជុំកោះសេប៊ូ

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that during a recent UN Security Council meeting, they informed Thailand of their willingness to find a peaceful resolution to the border dispute to rebuild mutual trust.
title: Cambodia expresses readiness to solve border issue at UN after Thai incursion

summary: This article reflects on the one-year anniversary of the May 28 border clash at the 'Emerald Triangle' (Mom Bei/Chong Bok), detailing how it escalated into a major crisis involving troop deployments, diplomatic standoffs, and the deaths of soldiers. It notes that while a ceasefire exists, the border remains tense.
title: May 28 border skirmish has grown into a regional flashpoint

summary: At a UN Security Council session, Cambodian Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn and his Thai counterpart discussed border friction. Sokhonn called for the effective implementation of the December 2025 peace agreement, while the Thai side reaffirmed its commitment to the ceasefire and rejected claims of territorial ambition.
title: Cambodia and Thailand trade barbs over border at UN session

summary: The Cambodian National Assembly has welcomed a European Parliament recommendation urging Cambodia and Thailand to resolve their ongoing border disputes through peaceful diplomatic dialogue, international frameworks, and existing bilateral commissions.
title: NA welcomes EU call for peaceful border row resolution

summary: This article marks the one-year anniversary of the start of the current border tensions, noting that despite a fragile ceasefire, there is no comprehensive resolution. It mentions that Thai authorities are looking into building border walls, while Cambodia is seeking international legal intervention to settle the disputes along the undemarcated border.
title: One Year On and Cambodia-Thailand Border Tensions Remain Unresolved

summary: Following discussions in New York, Cambodia reaffirmed its commitment to working with Thailand to rebuild trust and implement the December 27, 2025 Joint Statement. Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn and Thai Prime Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow pledged to maintain regular communication to address the ongoing border dispute.
title: Cambodia ready to advance Thailand border pact

summary: The Prime Minister of Cambodia stated that border issues are caused by a small group of extremists who never show up on the battlefield, contrasting them with the soldiers and citizens affected by the conflict.
title: Border issues stemming from small group of extremists, says PM

summary: The Cambodian government urges Thailand to respect the commitments made during the General Border Committee (GBC) meetings to restore mutual trust and maintain peace, specifically rejecting any border claims made through military force or unilateral action.
title: Cambodia does not recognize border lines through use of force or unilateral claims by Thailand

summary: The Cambodian government has officially protested against Thailand, accusing them of violating sovereignty by expanding military infrastructure in disputed border areas, which Cambodia claims violates the December 2025 ceasefire agreement. The protest highlights the construction of roads, large Buddha statues, and the installation of shipping containers and barbed wire by Thai forces.
title: Cambodia exposes Thai military expansion in disputed territory

summary: The Cambodian government has formally protested recent construction activities by Thailand in disputed border areas, calling for a resumption of joint boundary commission work and a halt to unilateral territorial claims.
title: Cambodia protests Thai construction activities in occupied border areas
